=== ssh_proxy_cli 
exit 0
--- stdout
SSH SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli [command]

Commands:
  start [--foreground] [--wait=SECONDS]
      Start the proxy in the background
  restart [--foreground] [--wait=SECONDS]
      Restart with the current configuration
  stop
      Stop the proxy and its SSH tunnel
  status
      Show endpoint and health as JSON
  trust [ENDPOINT] [--check] [--log=FILE]
      Set up SSH login and host-key trust
  logs [--follow] [--lines=N]
      Show or follow proxy logs
  test [--url=URL]
      Test HTTP and SOCKS5 forwarding
  check
      Validate configuration as JSON

Service commands (current user):
  Use "ssh_proxy_cli service --help" for service details.

  service install
      Register and enable automatic startup
  service uninstall
      Stop and remove the service
  service status
      Show service state and automatic startup
  service enable
      Enable automatic startup
  service disable
      Disable automatic startup

Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)
  -h, --help          help for ssh_proxy_cli
  -v, --version       version for ssh_proxy_cli

Use "ssh_proxy_cli [command] --help" for command details.
--- stderr

=== ssh_proxy_cli start --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Start the proxy in the background

Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent; run trust for setup. After
--wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness. --wait
has no effect with --foreground.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli start [flags]

Flags:
      --foreground     Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  -h, --help           help for start
      --wait SECONDS   Wait up to SECONDS (1..3600) for background
                       readiness (default 20)

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)
--- stderr
=== ssh_proxy_cli restart -h
exit 0
--- stdout
Restart with the current configuration

Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent; run trust for setup. After
--wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness. --wait
has no effect with --foreground.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli restart [flags]

Flags:
      --foreground     Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  -h, --help           help for restart
      --wait SECONDS   Wait up to SECONDS (1..3600) for background
                       readiness (default 20)

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)

=== ssh_proxy_cli trust --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Set up SSH login and host-key trust. Without ENDPOINT, try SSH aliases in file
order until one succeeds. Verify host fingerprints before accepting. Already
working logins exit 0.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli trust [ENDPOINT] [flags]

Flags:
      --check      Check unattended login only: no prompts or new host
                   keys; the tray runs it before each start
  -h, --help       help for trust
      --log FILE   Append SSH diagnostics to FILE (used by the tray)

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)
--- stderr
=== ssh_proxy_cli logs --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Show or follow proxy logs

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli logs [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --follow    Follow new log lines
  -h, --help      help for logs
      --lines N   Show the last N (1..10000) lines (default 60)

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)
--- stderr

=== ssh_proxy_cli service bogus --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Manage the proxy service for the current user. Registration uses the current
user on every OS. Install enables automatic startup without starting the proxy;
run trust and confirm unattended login works, then stop the proxy before
installing. Enable/disable change automatic startup; use start, stop or restart
to run it. On macOS, re-enable a disabled service before starting it manually.
On Windows, install, uninstall, enable and disable need an elevated terminal,
and install prompts for your Windows password; on macOS and Linux run as the
current user, without sudo.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli service [flags]
  ssh_proxy_cli service [command]

Available Commands:
  install
      Register and enable automatic startup
  uninstall
      Stop and remove the service
  status
      Show service state and automatic startup
  enable
      Enable automatic startup
  disable
      Disable automatic startup

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for service

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)

Use "ssh_proxy_cli service [command] --help" for command details.
--- stderr

=== ssh_proxy_cli service install --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Register and enable automatic startup; install does not start the proxy.

Before installing, run trust and confirm unattended login works, then stop the
proxy. On Windows, run install in an elevated terminal; it prompts for your
Windows password. On macOS and Linux, run it as the current user, without sudo.
See "ssh_proxy_cli service --help" for details.

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli service install [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for install

Global Flags:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH (default: config.toml
                      beside the CLI)
